preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the glottal stop [ʔ] took place in Mẽbêngôkre (Kayapó) and Apinajé, two Trans-Tocantins languages of the Northern Jê branch. Nikulin (2020) states the change as *c > ʔ ~ ∅: the examples below show the glottal-stop outcome (Mẽbêngôkre ʔy 'seed', ʔi 'bone'), while in other words the consonant is lost altogether (*kacô 'to suck' > kaô). The Timbira languages have h in the same words.

examples.note: Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: c = voiceless palatal stop or coronal affricate, ĵ = its voiced counterpart, ñ = [ɲ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], ô/ê = close-mid vowels.
In other words the reflex is zero, as in kaô from *kacô 'to suck'.
Here the glottal stop survives between vowels; Parkatêjê has kuhõ.

sources: Nikulin, A. (2020). Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/38893
